steps.title: Made for food
steps.body: Sangiovese's acidity makes it perfect with tomato: pasta al pomodoro, pizza, lasagne. Its tannin suits grilled meat, like bistecca alla fiorentina, a thick T-bone. Brunello suits wild boar, game and aged pecorino. It's one of the most food-dependent reds; it can taste austere alone.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 16 to 18 degrees. Chianti Classico Annata is best within five years. Riserva and Gran Selezione age 10 to 20 years. Brunello ages 15 to 30 years, gaining leather, tobacco and dried cherry. Decant young Brunello.

steps.explanation: A classic Tuscan match for Chianti or Brunello.

steps.body: If a Sangiovese tastes austere on its own, try it with a bite of tomato pasta. Its acidity and tannin will suddenly make sense.

steps.explanation: Sweet desserts make it taste sour.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Its tannin suits grilled meat and aged cheese
